notes: Shopify storefront, HTTP-fetch worked fully (robots.txt: 'Allow: /', no Claude-specific disallow; agents.md explicitly welcomes agentic crawling). Discovery: fetched sitemap.xml -> sitemap_collections_1.xml (472 collection URLs enumerated in full), fetched the rendered homepage mega-menu (all nav sections incl. 'Decor', 'Gifting'), cross-checked with internal search and 404-tested nonsense/likely-holiday slugs (diwali, christmas, holi, eid, navratri, easter, valentine, wedding-season, party-season, summer, winter, spring, autumn, and a nonsense slug all returned identical 404s -> confirms no dedicated hub pages for these and that the site's 404 behavior is consistent/trustworthy, no fake alias pages). Total catalog size = 1182 products (from /collections/all data-product-count, used as denominator for the generic-catalog-fraction check). Every candidate collection's qty was cross-checked via the theme's data-product-count attribute AND the Shopify /collections/<handle>/products.json product list -- both matched exactly in all cases. The site has ONE 'Gifting by Occasion' mega-menu section (visible in nav + confirmed in homepage SEO copy: 'Check out gifting online... whether it is birthday gifting, housewarming gifting, anniversary gift, gifts for him and her, festive gifts for festivals like Durga Puja, Dussehra, Diwali, Christmas, or New Year') that lists Diwali Gifts, Christmas Gifts, New Year Gifts, Rakhi Gifts, Valentine's Day Gifts, Father's/Mother's Day Gifts, Friendship Day Gifts, Bhai Dooj Gifts, Onam, Festivals, Lohri/Sakranti Gifts and Independence Day AS SIBLINGS of clearly non-seasonal occasions (Birthday Gifts, Anniversary Gifts, Wedding Gifts, Housewarming Gifts, Farewell Gifts, Gifts for Him/Her). Sampled full product lists (not just titles) of every one of these: mothers-day (88), father-s-day (4), friendship-day-gifts (38), diwali-gifts (11), christmas-gifts (133), bhai-dooj-gifts (15), onam (13), rakhi-gifting (98), valentines-day (12), new-year-gifts (40), festivals (60), lohri-sakranti-gifts (0), independence-day (0). Every non-empty one of these is built from the SAME shared pool of plain generic tableware/kitchenware/decor SKUs (mugs, jar candles, cake stands, glass cloches, ecomix sculptures, platters, water bottles, planters) -- e.g. 'Posed Dove Ecomix Accent - White' appears in mothers-day, bhai-dooj-gifts, valentines-day, onam and rakhi-gifting simultaneously; 'Maya large t-light holder' appears in mothers-day, christmas-gifts, festivals and diwali-gifts simultaneously; 'Fleur D'or Candle Stand - Large' appears in diwali-gifts, christmas-gifts, festivals and rakhi-gifting simultaneously. None of the products in any of these collections is Diwali/Christmas/Valentine/Rakhi/Onam-specific merchandise (no ornaments, no rakhi threads, no boat/pookalam Onam items, no heart-shaped Valentine products) -- they are a generic 'gift-appropriate home decor' catalog re-tagged under many different occasion-named URLs including non-seasonal ones (Birthday, Anniversary, Housewarming), which is exactly the generic-catalog-under-a-holiday-URL trap this extraction is required to guard against. All 13 were therefore excluded as marketing gift-occasion collections, not genuine seasonal PLPs, even though several (diwali-gifts, christmas-gifts, valentines-day, rakhi-gifting, onam, new-year-gifts) have holiday names in their URL/title. Also checked and excluded for the same/related reasons: urli (3 products, meta description only says 'traditional accents', no festival association), pooja-accessories (1 product, generic pooja/ritual items, not Diwali-specific), wax-filled-diya (4 products, meta description says 'festivals' generically not Diwali specifically, and 1 of its 4 products already duplicates a product in the diyas collection -- treated as a redundant material-facet slice of Diyas rather than a distinct genuine branch). The one genuine Diwali category found: /collections/diyas, filed under the normal 'Decor > Table Decor' taxonomy branch (not the Gifting menu), page title 'Diya - Buy Handcraft Decorative Diyas Online at Best Price in India', meta description explicitly states 'Perfect for Diwali, festive decor, pooja, and gifting', and its 9 products are unambiguously Diwali diya lamps (Gaudeep Gulzar Diya Set of 21, Aarambh Terracotta Diya Set of 21, Gaudeep Gold Stripes Diya Set of 12, Gaudeep Gold Diya Set of 12, Kanchdeep Wax Filled Diya Set of 24, Gaudeep Diya Set of 24, Kanchdeep Diya Set of 24, Trigun Terracotta Diya Set, Shathdeep Handmade Diya Set of 24) -- bulk sets of 12-24 diyas, consistent with Diwali home-lighting use rather than daily single-diya pooja use. Checked specifically for Holi and Raksha Bandhan per task instructions: no Holi collection exists anywhere on the site (not in the 472-URL sitemap, /collections/holi returns 404 same as a nonsense slug); Raksha Bandhan is present only as 'rakhi-gifting' under the generic Gifting menu, already excluded above as a generic-catalog gift-occasion page (98 products, same shared decor pool, no rakhi thread/pooja-thali specific merchandise). Checked for Eid, Navratri, Dussehra, Ganesh Chaturthi, Janmashtami, Karwa Chauth, Makar Sankranti (beyond the Lohri/Sakranti empty gift collection), Baisakhi, Durga Puja, Easter, Thanksgiving: none appear anywhere in the 472-collection sitemap or main navigation. No PDP crawling was performed; classification was based on collection-level product listings, meta descriptions and site navigation/taxonomy structure only.

rows.evidence: Page meta description: 'Explore handcrafted diyas by Ellementry, designed to illuminate your home with warmth and elegance. Perfect for Diwali, festive decor, pooja, and gifting.'
